prize_parts.citation: for the invention and development of optical lattice clocks based on magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms, which brought optical frequency measurement to the 10^-18 level

statement.case_for: I keep B010 for Katori and Ye as a single part and have not changed my preferred configuration since round 1. Having read the full exchange, the case rests on three points that survived the objections. First, the invention is specific: Katori's magic-wavelength lattice removes the trap-induced shift of the clock transition, so many neutral atoms can be interrogated at once, which is a different route to stability from single-ion clocks and from the comb. Second, the outcome is measured and reproduced: fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, beyond the caesium definition of the second, confirmed in several independent laboratories with Sr, Yb and other species, and already used for redshift measurements over millimetre distances and for limits on variation of constants. Third, the credit is the cleanest on the shortlist, since no member proposed any other pair. The citation must name the lattice scheme and neutral atoms, and must not mention the pending redefinition of the second, as Lindroth and Kroll both argue. I weigh measurement capability as a legitimate criterion, because instruments of this kind change what can be tested, but I do not claim it outranks a new organising concept in matter. My preference is for the candidate whose science and attribution are both settled today.
statement.case_against: The reservations that remain are real. Whether a lattice-clock prize reads as a further stage of the line recognised in 2005 and 2012 is a judgement the citation wording can shape but cannot remove, and Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig have not said that the lattice distinction satisfies them. The two names leave out Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto, Derevianko and the ion-clock groups, and the relative weight of Katori's proposal against Ye's accuracy programme is not settled by the supplied material. B047 has the broader opening support among top-three placements and rests on a conceptual change in how insulators are classified, and I cannot say that a measurement achievement outweighs that on scientific grounds alone. If the committee judges that a discovery of new physics must take precedence over a measurement advance, B047 or B051 would be the better prize.

responses.point: Mehlig keeps B047 first as a conceptual change, namely a topological invariant replacing a broken symmetry, supported by fifteen years of confirmation, and raises a two-part configuration in which B047 is paired with a precision or quantum-technology achievement. He also admits that the credit leaves out Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and the 3D work.
responses.response: I accept the conceptual weight of B047 and do not dispute its maturity. A two-part prize combining B047 and B010 would carry five people, and the rule limits any configuration to three, so it cannot be proposed in the form you suggest. The choice is therefore between the two on their merits. My reason to prefer B010 is that its credit is settled by the pair of names that every supporter gives, while you yourself state that whichever three names are chosen for B047, visible contributors are left out and the 3D chapter is arguably separate. I would not oppose B047 if the committee prefers it, and I have listed it as my first alternative.

responses.point: Danielsson holds B051 first, as a prediction followed by observation, and asks for a citation that honours the observed correlated and superconducting states without asserting a pairing mechanism, accepting that Cao is outside the three names. He also says that the clock toolbox was already recognised.
responses.response: Your question on novelty is the one I take most seriously. The magic-wavelength condition is not a property of combs or of trapped ions, since it concerns the engineering of a lattice in which the clock transition is unperturbed to the required level for many neutral atoms at once. That is why I would insist on citation wording about the lattice scheme and neutral atoms. On B051, I accept that your proposed citation avoids a claim on the mechanism, which meets part of my maturity concern. The omission of Cao from a three-name cap would still be visible, and the theory-plus-experiment trio does not cover the many groups that reproduced the states. I prefer B010, but I would not call B051 an unreasonable choice.

responses.point: Kroll supports B010, calls the redefinition of the second timing in favour, and discloses a research stay in Hall's laboratory in Boulder, asking the committee to judge whether that requires recusal on B010.
responses.response: I agree that the citation should not lean on the redefinition. On your disclosure, a doctoral research stay in the laboratory of a 2005 laureate is adjacent to the B010 credit and not part of it, and it does not make you a collaborator of Katori or Ye. I would not ask you to withhold a vote, but the committee record should show the disclosure, and the weight of your support should be read with it in mind. This matters because four members now support B010, and I am one of them.

responses.point: Eriksson prefers B047 with Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, and says Mele should stay in place of Hasan as the origin of the Z2 invariant. He also says that the 2016 prize leaves the committee needing to state why the quantum spin Hall effect is distinct.
responses.response: I agree that Mele belongs with Kane, since the Z2 papers are joint, and I do not think Hasan should displace him. My remaining difficulty with B047 is narrower than the 2016 question, which you, Mehlig and Johansson argue convincingly turns on time-reversal symmetry and spin-orbit coupling. It is that the experimental credit falls on Molenkamp alone while the HgTe prediction came from Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and no wording of the citation settles that. If the committee can write it so that the prediction is credited to the Z2 theory and the observation to the HgTe experiment, I would find B047 a defensible prize.

responses.point: Olsson moved to B010 from B039 and raises whether the committee should wait for the formal redefinition of the second before recognising lattice clocks.
responses.response: I do not think waiting improves the case. The performance exists, is reproduced, and is already in use for fundamental tests, whereas the redefinition is a decision of the metrological community that may follow its own schedule and does not enter the science. Waiting would also tie the committee to a process outside its control. I agree with Kroll and Lindroth that the pending redefinition should stay out of the citation, so that the award rests on the invention and the measured accuracy, and not on a forecast.

responses.point: Johansson prefers B047, names B046 as a cleaner alternative if the B047 allocation cannot be settled, and holds that the three-dimensional work may be better treated as a later prize. He recuses from any circuit QED decision.
responses.response: I agree with you that if the committee cannot settle the 2D and 3D allocation, a simpler configuration is better than a contested trio, and that is the same reasoning that leads me to B010. On B046, Cirac and Zoller is a strong proposal, but it was ranked by only three members and the committee has not argued it through, so I would not bring it forward at this stage. I note your recusal on B041 and agree that circuit QED should stay out this year.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts the magic-wavelength lattice as separate from the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize. Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig have not said whether it does.

Whether Katori and Ye can be credited without Lemonde, Ludlow, Takamoto, Derevianko or the ion-clock groups, and how to weigh the proposal against the accuracy programme. I rely on my recollection of the priority history and have not verified it from documents.

Whether a measurement-capability achievement should carry the same weight as the conceptual reclassification in B047. I have not settled this myself, and it is the main reason B047 remains my first alternative.
Whether the B047 credit can be settled in a form that the committee finds fair, which would change my view of the choice between B010 and B047.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B010, B047 or B051. My documented connections are to PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur, and none involves the credited names. Astroparticle physics is adjacent to B061 (IceCube), which I no longer advocate, and I would stand back from any final decision on it. I note Kroll's disclosure on B010 and that I am one of the four members supporting that candidate.
